# OneMind TAK NATS leaf node.
# The nats-bridge plugin connects to this leaf in plaintext (in-cluster only).
# The leaf holds the ONEMIND leaf credentials + bus CA and remotes up to the
# DOKS bus leafnode port (7422) over TLS. Plugin stays creds-free and portable:
# same plugin config works on Mac / DOKS / edge — only the leaf's remote changes.
#
# Secret `tak-nats-leaf` (leaf.conf + ca.crt) is created out-of-band (contains the
# leaf_tak password) — see DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md. Never committed.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tak-nats-leaf
  namespace: takserver
  labels: { app: tak-nats-leaf }
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: tak-nats-leaf } }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: { app: tak-nats-leaf }
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: nats
          image: nats:2.10-alpine
          args: ["-c", "/etc/leaf/leaf.conf"]
          ports:
            - { containerPort: 4222, name: client }
            - { containerPort: 8222, name: monitor }
          volumeMounts:
            - { name: leaf, mountPath: /etc/leaf, readOnly: true }
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: 8222 }
            initialDelaySeconds: 3
            periodSeconds: 10
          resources:
            requests: { cpu: 50m, memory: 32Mi }
            limits:   { cpu: 250m, memory: 128Mi }
      volumes:
        - name: leaf
          secret: { secretName: tak-nats-leaf }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: tak-nats-leaf
  namespace: takserver
  labels: { app: tak-nats-leaf }
spec:
  selector: { app: tak-nats-leaf }
  ports:
    - { name: client, port: 4222, targetPort: 4222, protocol: TCP }

apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: takserver-messaging-service
  namespace: takserver
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: Helm
  annotations:
    meta.helm.sh/release-name: takserver
    meta.helm.sh/release-namespace: takserver
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false,Delete=false,Replace=false,Force=false
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: '0'
spec:
  internalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  ipFamilies:
  - IPv4
  ipFamilyPolicy: SingleStack
  ports:
  - name: streaming-8089
    port: 8089
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 8089
  - name: fed-9000
    port: 9000
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 9000
  - name: fed-9001
    port: 9001
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 9001
  selector:
    app: takserver-messaging
  sessionAffinity: None
  type: ClusterIP

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
OneMind CoT Tap — TAK Server -> NATS bus (outbound / b3 outbound leg).

Connects to a TAK Server CoT streaming port (8089/ssl) as a mutual-TLS client
(exactly like an EUD), receives the full CoT firehose for its groups, and
republishes each <event>...</event> to a NATS subject (default tak.cot.out).

This exists because TAK's cluster plugin manager (PluginClusterMessenger) is
send-only: sender-receiver plugins can INJECT (bus->TAK) but never RECEIVE
(TAK->bus) across pods. The tap is the authoritative client-protocol path for
the outbound leg, decoupled from plugin-cluster internals.

Env:
  TAK_HOST         (default takserver-messaging)
  TAK_PORT         (default 8089)
  TAK_CERT         (default /certs/tap.pem)
  TAK_KEY          (default /certs/tap.key)
  TAK_CA           (default /certs/ca.pem)   # optional; verify off by default
  NATS_URL         (default nats://tak-nats-leaf:4222)
  NATS_SUBJECT     (default tak.cot.out)
  VERIFY_SERVER    (default "false")         # set "true" to verify server cert vs CA
"""
import asyncio
import os
import ssl
import sys
import logging

import nats

LOG = logging.getLogger("cot-tap")
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s",
    stream=sys.stdout,
)

TAK_HOST = os.getenv("TAK_HOST", "takserver-messaging")
TAK_PORT = int(os.getenv("TAK_PORT", "8089"))
TAK_CERT = os.getenv("TAK_CERT", "/certs/tap.pem")
TAK_KEY = os.getenv("TAK_KEY", "/certs/tap.key")
TAK_CA = os.getenv("TAK_CA", "/certs/ca.pem")
NATS_URL = os.getenv("NATS_URL", "nats://tak-nats-leaf:4222")
NATS_SUBJECT = os.getenv("NATS_SUBJECT", "tak.cot.out")
VERIFY_SERVER = os.getenv("VERIFY_SERVER", "false").lower() == "true"

EVENT_END = b"</event>"


def build_ssl_context() -> ssl.SSLContext:
    ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT)
    if VERIFY_SERVER and os.path.exists(TAK_CA):
        ctx.load_verify_locations(cafile=TAK_CA)
        ctx.check_hostname = False
        ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_REQUIRED
    else:
        ctx.check_hostname = False
        ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
    ctx.load_cert_chain(certfile=TAK_CERT, keyfile=TAK_KEY)
    return ctx


async def connect_nats():
    while True:
        try:
            nc = await nats.connect(
                NATS_URL,
                name="omos-cot-tap",
                max_reconnect_attempts=-1,
                reconnect_time_wait=2,
            )
            LOG.info("connected to NATS %s -> subject %s", NATS_URL, NATS_SUBJECT)
            return nc
        except Exception as e:
            LOG.error("NATS connect failed (%s); retry in 2s", e)
            await asyncio.sleep(2)


async def stream_tak(nc):
    ssl_ctx = build_ssl_context()
    reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection(TAK_HOST, TAK_PORT, ssl=ssl_ctx)
    LOG.info("TLS connected to TAK %s:%s", TAK_HOST, TAK_PORT)
    buf = b""
    count = 0
    try:
        while True:
            chunk = await reader.read(8192)
            if not chunk:
                LOG.warning("TAK stream closed by server")
                break
            buf += chunk
            # frame on </event>
            while True:
                idx = buf.find(EVENT_END)
                if idx == -1:
                    break
                end = idx + len(EVENT_END)
                raw = buf[:end]
                buf = buf[end:]
                start = raw.find(b"<event")
                if start == -1:
                    continue
                event = raw[start:]
                try:
                    await nc.publish(NATS_SUBJECT, event)
                    count += 1
                    if count <= 5 or count % 50 == 0:
                        LOG.info("published CoT #%d (%d bytes) to %s", count, len(event), NATS_SUBJECT)
                except Exception as e:
                    LOG.error("NATS publish failed: %s", e)
    finally:
        writer.close()
        try:
            await writer.wait_closed()
        except Exception:
            pass


async def main():
    LOG.info(
        "OneMind CoT Tap starting — TAK %s:%s -> NATS %s [%s]",
        TAK_HOST, TAK_PORT, NATS_URL, NATS_SUBJECT,
    )
    nc = await connect_nats()
    while True:
        try:
            await stream_tak(nc)
        except Exception as e:
            LOG.error("TAK stream error: %s", e)
        LOG.info("reconnecting to TAK in 3s...")
        await asyncio.sleep(3)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        asyncio.run(main())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass

# OneMind CoT Tap — TAK Server -> NATS bus (b3 outbound leg)
# Secret `cot-tap-certs` (tap.pem/tap.key/ca.pem) is created imperatively
# (out-of-band, never committed). See README.md.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cot-tap-script
  namespace: takserver
  labels:
    app: cot-tap
data:
  tap.py: |
    # placeholder — overwritten by: kubectl create configmap cot-tap-script --from-file=tap.py
    # (kept in git as tak-cluster/cot-tap/tap.py; apply with kustomize/kubectl replace)
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cot-tap
  namespace: takserver
  labels:
    app: cot-tap
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cot-tap
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cot-tap
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: cot-tap
          image: python:3.12-slim
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
          args:
            - "pip install --no-cache-dir --quiet nats-py && exec python /app/tap.py"
          env:
            - name: TAK_HOST
              value: "takserver-messaging-service"
            - name: TAK_PORT
              value: "8089"
            - name: TAK_CERT
              value: "/certs/tap.pem"
            - name: TAK_KEY
              value: "/certs/tap.key"
            - name: TAK_CA
              value: "/certs/ca.pem"
            - name: NATS_URL
              value: "nats://tak-nats-leaf:4222"
            - name: NATS_SUBJECT
              value: "tak.cot.out"
            - name: VERIFY_SERVER
              value: "false"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: script
              mountPath: /app
            - name: certs
              mountPath: /certs
              readOnly: true
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 25m
              memory: 64Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 200m
              memory: 128Mi
      volumes:
        - name: script
          configMap:
            name: cot-tap-script
        - name: certs
          secret:
            secretName: cot-tap-certs

# Pinned Node-RED + TAK conversion image

This is an image source, not a published image or a live integration. Node-RED's
supported distribution is its [official container](https://nodered.org/docs/getting-started/docker).
The upstream project does not publish a supported Helm chart; OneMind supplies
ordinary Kubernetes manifests through Argo rather than adopting a community chart.

| Input | Pin |
| --- | --- |
| Official Node-RED + Node.js | `nodered/node-red:5.0.9-24@sha256:e085d4a06591fd0aca2ea2a91364d27f1a0e31e885675f77935e10f95412a963` |
| TAK converter | `node-red-contrib-tak@4.2.2`, npm integrity in `package-lock.json` |
| TAK upstream source / npm gitHead | [`490e3801b76f5737a6e021297b5efad9c9ca5042`](https://github.com/snstac/node-red-contrib-tak/tree/490e3801b76f5737a6e021297b5efad9c9ca5042) |
| Proposed publication | `ghcr.io/onemindos/nodered-tak:5.0.9-tak4.2.2-r1` |

Pins checked 2026-10-24 against upstream releases, the anonymous Docker registry
manifest index, npm package metadata and the tagged source. The lock fixes the
converter's transitive dependencies too. npm lifecycle scripts are disabled.
The dev-only Node-RED package supports a real local authentication/palette smoke
test; production retains the official image's runtime and installs only the
converter dependency tree into `/opt/onemind-nodes`.
Production omits dev, peer and optional dependencies so the converter's optional
Node-RED peer does not install a second runtime; the official base provides it.

`bootstrap.cjs` links the reviewed module into `/data/node_modules`, seeds an empty
flow file only if absent, and refuses to replace a conflicting installed module.
It does not overwrite flows, credentials, settings or context. Settings are loaded
from the immutable image, outside `/data`. Every restart uses `--safe`; a deliberate
authenticated Deploy is required to start flows. The disabled example is bundled
under `/opt/onemind/examples` and in Git, never imported automatically.

The TAK package encodes/decodes CoT; it does not itself enroll with or connect to a
TAK Server. The three converter outputs include binary protocol forms. The example
connects only the JSON output to a local debug node, with manual inject, no repeat,
no TCP/MQTT/NATS/HTTP transport, and a disabled tab.

## Build and verify

```bash
cd services/nodered-tak
npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
npm test
docker build -t onemind-nodered-tak:smoke .
node test/image-smoke.cjs
```

Use Node.js 24. npm 12 may additionally require `--allow-remote=all` for the
dev-only upstream Node-RED npm dependency's pinned npm tarball; this is a
per-command install option, not a change to provider or credential configuration.
The real-runtime smoke test creates only loopback HTTP traffic and ephemeral test
credentials in process memory, and deletes its temporary user directory afterward.
The image smoke test requires Docker, checks the actual read-only container and
TAK palette with ephemeral memory-only credentials, then removes its own container.
Neither test connects to TAK or an event bus.

`.github/workflows/build-nodered-tak.yml` builds and tests on pull requests without
publishing. After review/merge, a coordinator may explicitly dispatch the workflow
on `main` with `publish=true`. It tests the image before publication, publishes the
version tag and source-SHA tag, and records an immutable GHCR digest in the run
summary. Publication is restricted to that explicit main-branch dispatch. The
workflow uses the repository's `GITHUB_TOKEN`; no new registry credentials belong
in Git. Confirm GHCR pull visibility/permissions before activation; a private image
needs a separately sealed app-namespace pull Secret and Deployment reference.

Before the deployment change is activated, replace its version-tag reference with
the actual `ghcr.io/onemindos/nodered-tak@sha256:...` reported by the successful
build. No application-image digest has been invented or claimed verified here.
The first commit can be integrated independently to publish this image before the
manual deployment commit. [Deployment, enrollment and recovery gates](../../platform/nodered/README.md).
